# Design Decisions — canonical owner decision ledger

This is the **flat, greppable canonical ledger** for owner semantic and
architecture decisions. It holds both SETTLED rulings and OPEN owner questions,
so agents do not re-litigate settled work or silently implement an unanswered
proposal (`OWNER-LEDGER:` — the authority is the row, never this paragraph). One row per decision: the ruling/proposal + a pointer to its detail
doc and/or owner-memory note.

Rules of the road:

- **A row here is the ruling.** If code, a test, or a `.css` test-data file
  disagrees with a SETTLED row, the code/test/data is what changes — not the
  ruling. Confirm against the linked detail before acting.
- **OPEN rows are explicitly not settled** — they record the current state of a
  live thread so nobody mistakes silence for a decision.
- **"Source" pointers** are relative paths inside this dir unless prefixed
  `memory:` (a note in the owner's project memory,
  `.claude/projects/-Users-matthew-git-oss-jess/memory/<name>.md`).

## Ledger process (PROPOSED)

Every owner question that can alter parser facts, AST shape, lookup, evaluation,
or emitted CSS gets an `OPEN` row here before implementation. Its linked detail
record must state the exact owner proposal, known unknowns, and required
invariants/tests. The owner changes only the row's status/ruling when deciding;
the implementing agent then links the landed code and tests. Superseded rows
remain with their status and replacement pointer rather than being deleted.

## 0. The epistemics — there is NO external authority (read first)

Correctness is **the documented intended v5 design**, nothing else. The less.js
`alpha` top-level `.css` test-data AND the Jess tests are _imperfect encodings_
of that design — kept up to date toward it, and wrong as often as the engine is.
When the engine disagrees with a `.css` file, the question is "which matches the
intended design?" — then reconcile the loser TO the design. Do not treat any
file as an authority to blindly match.

Owner also **banned the authoritative-reference framing words** — say "the intended
design" / "the expected `.css` output" / "reconcile the test-data to the design."
Several existing docs (`REFERENCE.md`, `EXTEND-SEMANTICS.md`,
`GOAL1-SCORECARD.md`, and many spec headers) still use the banned framing; treat
their _content_ as valid consistency-check guidance, but their _"authoritative
reference"_ framing is superseded by this row. Source:
`memory:intended-design-is-truth` (owner 2026-07-17).

| J14 | **Import-once drops a `(reference)` re-import of a sheet already imported plainly**, as Less 4.x does: `@import "t.less"; @import (reference) "t.less"; .x:extend(.sm) {}` renders only `.sm, .x { b: 2; }`. Coherence: import-once means one placement of a sheet's rules, and a `(reference)` import asks for nothing visible, so once a plain import has placed the sheet visibly the re-import adds only a hidden second copy whose sole effect would be to duplicate the blocks an extend reveals (`.x { b: 2; }` next to `.sm, .x { b: 2; }`). A `(multiple)` import, or one inside a `(multiple)` sheet, places its own copy. The other orderings are ruled by X18 (2026-10-06). **Import-once counts only a copy placed in the SAME scope (SETTLED — orchestrator judgment under owner delegation 2026-10-07; principle O17).** A scope is the root, one ruleset or one at-rule block. A mixin call, applied ruleset, detached-ruleset call or loop iteration imports into the scope it runs in, and an imported sheet's root belongs to its importer's scope. `.wrap { @import "t"; } @import "t";` and `@media print { @import "t"; } @import "t";` render the root copy and make its mixins callable at the root; lessc 4.9.1 drops the root import and leaves `.mx` undefined. The rule applies both ways: `@import "t"; @media print { @import "t"; }` places a second copy inside `@media print`. This moves the strict-imports golden, registered in pending-golden-edits.ts. Each scope's copy is its own extend placement. `.m() { @import "t"; } .m(); @import "t";` and `.a { .m(); .m(); }` place `t` once; `.x { .m(); } .y { .m(); }` places it twice. An `@import` of a sheet that an enclosing `@import` is still placing is a no-op in every scope, so a sheet that imports itself, directly or through other sheets, ends: `s.less` = `.s{a:1} .x{@import "s.less"}` gives `.s{a:1}`. lessc's recursion detector gives the same. The entry document is not on that stack: it is not placed by an `@import`, so an entry that imports itself inside `.x` places one copy there, as before. **Cycle and bare-`&` amendment (SETTLED — orchestrator judgment under owner delegation 2026-10-07):** a `(multiple)` import of a sheet an enclosing `@import` is still placing is an `import/cycle` error, since each copy would import another without end (`ms.less` = `.s { a: 1; } @import (multiple) "ms.less";` overflowed the stack; lessc 4.9.1 does not finish on it either). Any other import of such a sheet stays a no-op, one inside a `(multiple)` sheet included. A rule whose selector is a bare `&`, guarded or not, writes into its parent's selector, so it is not a scope of its own: it imports into its parent's import-once scope (`& when (@c) { @import "t"; } @import "t";` writes `t` once; `.x { & { @import "t"; } @import "t"; }` writes `.x .t` once). A ruleset around the `&` rule is still its own scope. | SETTLED — orchestrator judgment under owner delegation 2026-10-05; same-scope amendment orchestrator judgment under owner delegation 2026-10-07; cycle and bare-`&` amendment the same day | jess#359; X13; `EXTEND-SEMANTICS.md` §11; `packages/core/src/ast/serialize.ts` `isReferenceReimport`, `importIsNoOp`, `importCycles`, `importScopeOf`, `Frame.importScope`, `Emit.importsExpanding`; `packages/jess/test/less/import-once-scope.test.ts`; `packages/jess/test/less/extend-cross-import.test.ts` |
| J15 | **A body-form `&:extend()` written directly in a mixin definition is carried on the `MixinDefinition` (`extendInstructions`) and applied by each call site to the rule the call's body lands in**, as lessc copies the Extend into the caller. The same holds for a ruleset called as a mixin, with or without parentheses (`.m{&:extend(.sm); c:d} .x{.m;}` extends `.x` too), and for a rule nested in a mixin body, which extends as its composed selector (`.m(){.y{&:extend(.sm)}} .x{.m();}` → `.sm, .x .y`). A call outside every rule extends nothing; an inline `:extend()` on a called ruleset's selector stays its own. | SETTLED — orchestrator judgment under owner delegation 2026-10-05 | settles X16; jess#356; `EXTEND-SEMANTICS.md` §2, §6; `packages/core/src/ast/serialize.ts` `recordCalledExtends`; `packages/syntax/less/less-parser/src/grammar.ts` `MixinDefinitionContinuation`; `packages/jess/test/less/mixin-public-semantics.test.ts` |

| J16 | **A paren group around a single value that nothing computes keeps its parens in every dialect**: `c: (10vh)`, `var(--a, (10px))`, `($(10px))`, a group around a call written out as-is, and math kept as written. "Computes" means: math that operates; a comparison at a `.jess` `$( … )` boundary; a call that a callable runs (`(percentage(0.5))`, `.jess` `($percentage(0.5))`); an `if()`; and anything a reference names that is one of these, however it is read (variable, `@@name`, mixin parameter, `$prop`, map, namespace or mixin-call member). A kept group only changes the spelling: math, comparisons and callables still read the value inside it. For example, SCSS `@function g() { @return (1px); }` gives `g() + g()` → `2px`. F4 (grouping parens dissolve once computed) is the other half of this rule. **Reach (amended; orchestrator judgment under owner delegation 2026-10-06):** a paren group around one value that a reference reached evaluates to its value wherever the reference is read: values, selector and string interpolations, math functions (`calc(@a * 2)` → `calc(10px * 2)`), media and container queries (`(min-width: @a)` → `(min-width: 10px)`), and map, namespace and mixin-call members. A group around a call counts as one value (`@a: (var(--y)); .x-@{a}` → `.x-var(--y)`). A group written directly in a declaration value, or written inside a math function around a value nothing computes, keeps its parens even inside a reached value (`@c: calc(1px + (10px))` keeps `(10px)`); inside a math function a group whose content computes loses its parens (owner 2026-10-07, see P35). **Resolved means resolved (SETTLED — orchestrator judgment under owner delegation 2026-10-07; replaces the earlier ‘text a call returns’ paragraph and its more-than-one-value byte test):** parens are dropped when the calculation in them is resolved. Text is never a resolved calculation: a group around an escaped string (`~"…"`, `e()`, `escape()`, an interpolated template, the text an `if()` picks, a .jess `$e()`) keeps its parens wherever the group is read, however long the text is, a variable reaching it included: `calc(2 * (e("1px + 2px")))` → `calc(2 * (1px + 2px))`, `@t: (e("1px + 2px")); calc(2 * @t)` → `calc(2 * (1px + 2px))`, `(e("foo"))` → `(foo)`, `calc(2 * (e("foo")))` → `calc(2 * (foo))`. The test is the value's type (the value-domain `Any`, V3), never its bytes; the byte scanners `isLooseText`/`isLooseValue` and `looseParens` are deleted. A reference that resolves to one value is a resolved calculation, which amends ‘computes’ above: a group around a variable, parameter, property or member that names one value drops its parens (`@a: 10vh; width: (@a)` → `width: 10vh`, `calc(2 * (@a))` → `calc(2 * 10vh)`, SCSS `@return ($x)` writes `c: f(1px)` → `1px`). A reference naming a list keeps them (`calc(100% / (@v))` with `@v: 50vh/2` → `calc(100% / (50vh / 2))`), as does one naming a call written out as-is. A Sass calculation (a `.scss` `calc()`, `ValueEvaluator.sassCalculations`, set by the SCSS plugin) treats an unquoted string as text too, so it keeps a group around one, as dart-sass does (`calc(2 * (unquote("1px + 2px")))`, `calc(2 * ($k))` with `$k: foo`); outside one, SCSS parens around a resolved value drop, as in dart-sass (`(unquote("foo"))` → `foo`, `($d)` → `10px`). Code: `packages/core/src/ast/serialize.ts` `isOpaqueText`, `textGroup`, `reachedGroup`, `keepAuthoredGroup`, `slotComputation`; `value-eval.ts` `ValueEvaluator.sassCalculations`. | V6  | **Value arithmetic runs in EXACT BASE 10 for `+`, `-`, `*`, `%`; `/` and the transcendental fns stay on FLOAT.** A CSS author writes decimals, IEEE-754 stores binary, and a terminating decimal such as `0.1` or `0.33333333333333` is a repeating binary fraction. Chained arithmetic accumulates that error and, on subtracting near-equal quantities, cancels away the significant digits: three chained `fadeout(#f00, 33.333333333333%)` landed 1.2% from the true decimal `1e-14` and emitted `rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.00000000000000988098492)`. Every float step there is CORRECTLY ROUNDED (measured: 0 ulp error per step), so the loss is the BASE, not the operation — no reassociation, operand reordering, or multiply-by-complement recovers it. Implemented with `big.js` at the two accumulation points: `calculate()` in `packages/core/src/ast/value-operate.ts` and the alpha fns in `packages/fns`. **This is not a rounding step and does not touch V4/V5** — exact arithmetic REMOVES error where a construction-time round ADDS it. **`/` is excluded on CORRECTNESS grounds, not perf:** big.js `div` rounds to `Big.DP` DECIMAL PLACES (20), not significant digits, so `1e-15 / 3` yields `3.3333e-16` (5 sig digits) against float's `3.3333333333333336e-16` (17) — the same class of mistake as the 8-dp floor removed in `f42decf7f`/`137cfa8fa`, and no fixed `DP` fixes it because `DP` is absolute while magnitudes are not. There is also nothing to preserve: a quotient of terminating decimals is generally non-terminating. big.js has no `sin`/`cos`/`tan`/`log` and rejects a fractional `pow` exponent, so those fns stay float necessarily. **Integer operands take a float fast path** (exact below 2^53, so base 10 buys nothing). **No source-text plumbing is required:** `String(double)` is the shortest round-tripping decimal (verified: 0 failures in 200k random doubles), so `Big(0.33333333333333)` and `Big('0.33333333333333')` are the same value and a parsed double recovers its authored decimal. **Scope measured, not assumed:** the whole less.js unit corpus (136 files, 140 KB, 1647 emitted declarations) executes **280** scalar arithmetic ops — 0.17 per declaration, 2.05 per source KB; `benchmark.less` 2184 ops against 3478 declarations. Arithmetic is 3-4 orders of magnitude off the parse hot path, so a per-op branch to keep a float tier was not worth its three correctness guards. **Sibling colour ops deliberately NOT converted:** `lighten`/`darken`/`saturate`/`desaturate`/`spin` accumulate on HSL channels that `colorHsl` derives as `rgb/255`, and `128/255 = 0.5019607843137255…` does NOT terminate in base 10 either (255 has the prime factor 17) — base 10 would relocate their rounding, not remove it. They need a rational/exact-ratio model, which is a numeric-model change and a separate owner decision. | SETTLED (owner 2026-07-30; landed) | this ledger; `packages/core/src/ast/value-operate.ts`, `packages/fns/src/util/decimal.ts`, `packages/fns/src/less/__tests__/alpha-precision.test.ts` |
| V7  | **A non-finite computed number is an EVALUATION ERROR — `NaN` and `infinity` must never reach emitted CSS.** Neither is a CSS `<number>`, so emitting one writes a declaration the browser drops, silently. The rule is stated over the CONSTRUCT (a computed number), not over the functions that happened to produce it, and is enforced ONCE at the output boundary `formatNumber` (`packages/core/src/ast/format-number.ts`) — the single site every computed number crosses — so no future NaN-producing path can leak either. `serializeDimension` no longer spells `NaN`/`infinity`/`-infinity`; that spelling WAS the leak. Consequences: `sqrt(-4)`, `asin(2)`, `acos(2)`, `pow(-1, .5)` and `mod(1, 0)` now FAIL the call, so `functionMode` decides the output (default `preserve` → verbatim call bytes; `error` → `Invalid function call`, matching 4.x's rejection); an arithmetic overflow (`1e400 + 1`) is a hard eval error, since it is not a call and has no `functionMode` to fall back to. Un-operated literals are untouched by V1 — `x: 1e999px` still emits verbatim. A non-finite `Dimension` is therefore UNCONSTRUCTIBLE, which deletes `extract`'s non-finite-index branch as dead code. **Applied to plugin transport (2026-10-05):** a `@use` JS function or legacy `@plugin` function that returns a non-finite number is refused in the worker before JSON turns it into `null`, and reported at the call: `eval/invalid-function` for a namespaced `@use` call, `plugin/function-threw` for `@plugin`. An in-process Less plugin's `NaN` is reported the same way. | SETTLED (landed 2026-07-30) | `packages/core/src/ast/format-number.ts`, `packages/core/src/ast/serialize-value.ts`; `docs/state/less-4x-function-triage.md` §7-A |

EQUALITY NEVER RAISES (RESOLVED-SEMANTICS §4.1, owner 2026-08-01): `$(1em = 1px)` and `$(1em == 1px)` are `false` in every mode, and only an ORDER over units that do not reconcile raises under `strict` (§4.2; dart-sass raises too). A `$( … )` is the same computation wherever its value is read, inside `calc()` included, directly or through a variable (F8). The default is a dialect default (`jess-plugin-jess` `dialectDefaults` → `resolveOptions`), not a node fact. Per C19 (owner 2026-10-07) the default belongs to each file. A `.jess` file is strict under a `.less` entry, and a `.less` file keeps `preserve` under a `.jess` entry, also when its value is read through a variable from the other file. `.scss` keeps `preserve` until its math functions keep their operations as written (RESOLVED-SEMANTICS §6). This supersedes the OPEN text (`Operation.unitlessAdoptsUnit` as a `.scss`/`.jess`-only divergence, and "the single `.jess` answer is not chosen"). Dependencies are explicit (definition scope, params, `with(...)`, `@compose`) — this is the same direction `@compose` already took for imports (explicit composition, not ambient reads). Closes Less's caller-scope `fallback` READ at ALL body sites — `expandCall` mixin body (`serialize.ts:12412`), ruleset-mixin apply (`12636`), value-lambda `result:` (`4888`), detached ruleset (`13096`), partial application (`13777`/`13801`) — while KEEPING `fallback` for its non-read roles (R8 parent-exclusion recursion, caller-published-mixin visibility). **Distinct from the leak-OUT direction** (a mixin's private vars/rules leaking out so the caller can see them, R9): R16 is the caller→body READ and gets its OWN option **`allowCallerScope`** (`@default false` = lexical/hermetic; `true` = legacy Less dynamic caller-read). ## 6. Parsing & grammar

### 6.0 Codegen architecture — the four acceptance targets and the table design

**These are owner rulings. An agent that "reasons" its way to an objection here
is re-deriving something already settled with evidence — refute it from this
table, do not escalate it.** Measurements live in
`docs/state/GRAMMAR-SIZE-FACTS.md`.

| #   | Ruling | Status | Source / detail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| G1  | **Fastest compiled JS parser in the SVG comparison benchmarks** (chevrotain, nearley, peggy, parsimmon, jison, lezer × JSON/CSV/GraphQL), **excluding the incremental one**. A speed regression vs past parseman is **acceptable** if G2–G4 are met. | SETTLED (owner 2026-07-31) | supersedes the differential each-release-faster gate for this work |
| G2  | **Codegen ≤ 4× source bytes.** 10× is the absolute maximum tolerated; ~250 KB per compiled grammar ideally (aspirational, not pass/fail). Target the **per-dialect artifact a consumer downloads**; aggregate is bookkeeping only. | SETTLED (owner 2026-07-31) | `GRAMMAR-SIZE-FACTS.md` §2.3 — needs a **1.9×** call-site reduction, not 8–12× |
| G3  | **No factory pattern for multiple options.** Hot-swap, or cache the tables early. | SETTLED (owner 2026-07-31) | — |
| G4  | **One input grammar, one compiled output.** `trackLines` × `hostMode` handled inside the single artifact, not as four files. | SETTLED (owner 2026-07-31) | — |

Variants differ in **table contents, not in code**. A small startup cost is explicitly acceptable. | **SETTLED (owner, restated repeatedly)** | `GRAMMAR-SIZE-FACTS.md` §2.10a |

This binds hardest on defects a lane finds *outside* its own scope: a parseman defect found by a grammar lane is tasked to a parseman fix lane immediately (G12: grammars are parseman's showcase), and the finder documents and hands over rather than working around it. **Before closing ANY lane, list what it surfaced and name who owns each item.** | **SETTLED (owner 2026-07-31)** | owner: *"no reporting-only!! everything must have a follow-up action!"* |

| G22 | **A language construct we discover outside the parser suites gets a parser-suite fixture, in the same change.** The parser suites are the only instrument that runs on every commit; a one-off probe, a corpus sweep, a sass-spec triage and an oracle diff all run once and then stop watching. So a construct found by any of those routes and then fixed — with no fixture — is a defect that can silently return with nothing left to catch it. This binds regardless of outcome: if the construct now parses, pin the correct result; if it is still broken, **pin the current wrong result** with a `PINNED DEFECT` marker naming the defect, because a wrong answer that changes loudly beats a gap that changes silently. **A fix without a fixture is an incomplete change.** Backfill and marker convention: `packages/syntax/*/*-parser/test/discovered-constructs.test.ts`. | **SETTLED (owner 2026-07-31)** | owner: *"remember that each time we discover a language fixture we didn't CATCH (wasn't in parser tests) then it needs to be added to parser tests!!"* — raised after the same discovery route found and lost the same class of construct repeatedly in one day |
| G23 | **The coverage checklist is derived from the SPECS, never from the grammar.** G22 closes gaps one discovery at a time; it cannot find a construct nobody ever probed. A checklist read off the grammar can only report that the grammar covers what the grammar covers — the `@keyframes` case is the proof: a rewrite rejected **every** percentage keyframe selector and passed every suite, because no CSS fixture anywhere named the at-rule. So the construct space is enumerated from css-syntax-3, selectors-4, css-values-4 and the module specs, and **one table drives all four dialect gates**, because "valid CSS is valid in all four dialects" is one-way: a construct three dialects accept and the fourth rejects is a **defect in the fourth**, not a dialect difference, and a per-dialect expectation must never quietly absorb it. Coverage is measured mechanically, and the measurement states its own blind spots — a coverage claim from a method that cannot fail is worthless. Enumeration: `test/css-superset-corpus.ts`; gates: `packages/syntax/*/*-parser/test/css-superset-constructs.test.ts`. | **SETTLED (owner 2026-07-31)** | applies G22 proactively; first pass pinned 33 defects across the four dialects, incl. CDO/CDC rejected by all four and base-CSS rejecting namespaced attribute selectors that Less accepts |
| G24 | **Trivia lives in trivia. A production never disables trivia and re-defines it.** `noTrivia(...)` wrapped around a hand-spelled whitespace/comment regex is prohibited — not as a fallback, not as a stopgap, not when the ergonomic alternative is harder. The separator problem is not a separator problem, it is an **adjacency** problem, and it inverts: you never assert that trivia is present, you assert that two tokens are **not adjacent**. `1 - 2` — the `-` is not adjacent to the `2`, so subtraction. `1 -2` — adjacent, so a signed number in a space-separated list. `1/**/-/**/2` — not adjacent, and whether that is math is then a POLICY the production states rather than something a regex decides by accident. Expressed that way nothing needs to know what a separator looks like, so nothing can drift from the dialect's trivia table. If the mechanism's DX is bad, that is a **parseman task** — better parseman features to make this ergonomic are welcome; abusing parseman because the ergonomic path is harder is not. If adjacency genuinely cannot express a site, that is a finding to report, never a licence to fall back. | **SETTLED (owner 2026-07-31)** | owner: *"the FUCK, why does `expressionBoundary` even exist??? it looks like it's redefining trivia … trivia should be in trivia, not in expressions"*, then *"We already scoped an adjacency feature, and we can get rawChildren or whatever."* Already the settled parseman direction: `docs/design/derived-tokenization.md` §4 "Adjacency is a bit set at scan time (settled) [FOUNDATION]", and `src/compiler/token-scanner.ts` `tight`. This makes `nth(("a": 1), 1)` → `a 1` vs dart-sass `"a" 1` INTENDED, not a quote-dropping artifact. A bare word remains a Keyword even if CSS recognizes the same spelling as a named color: `red:` and `[red]:` are equal Keyword keys, while `[#c6538c]:` is a Color key. **Collections overlay with ordered shallow `...value;` spreads.** Items resolve left-to-right; a later Sass-equal key replaces the first matching entry without moving its position, and a new key appends. Duplicate explicit keys are valid and use the same later-wins rule. `jess/no-duplicate-collection-keys` warns only when two explicit keys in one literal are statically provable as equal; dynamic keys and spread contents are never guessed. Asked whether it matters that Less still treats the slash as a value when css/scss/jess no longer do: *“of course, why would we want that?”* Asked whether Less's division path should treat it as a separator before dividing: *“of course not”*. That is ledger P1 (math mode is a parse-time input; `/` parses to a different AST per mode) read correctly: ONE production parses the slash, and the mode chooses the SHAPE of its result — never which production gets the slash. So where the mode divides, the result is the division inside ONE `Expression` (the `$( … )` computation boundary, `core/src/ast/nodes.ts:329`); where it does not, the result is the slash-separated list `$(lhs) / $(rhs)` — each side its OWN `Expression`, so each side's own math still computes while the slash between them stays a separator. An earlier line here said Less does not adopt the slash-separated list; that was wrong and is withdrawn — the non-dividing result IS that list, of two expressions. MEASURED at `f570a9712`: the Less grammar does not wrap math in `Expression` today — its only `expression(` sites wrap CONDITIONS (`less-parser/src/grammar-helpers.ts:1263`) — so this is new structure, not a reshuffle; (3) a slash is always BETWEEN two operands in both models, so a leading slash still rejects in Less for the same structural reason it does in css. SECOND SYMPTOM TO CLEAR WITH IT: css's `ValueTerm` is inherited into the Less rule map and is UNREACHABLE there — dead weight in the compiled artifact, and the signal that Less has no slash rung. | P35 | **All Less math lowers into an `Expression` — the `$( … )` computation boundary — because in Jess that is the only place math happens.** Owner ruled 2026-09-23, verbatim: *“yes it's supposed to… because in Jess that's the only place we do math. .less -> .css and .less -> .jess -> .css needs to both work the same”*. So every Less operation the math mode COMPUTES reaches the AST inside an `Expression` (`core/src/ast/nodes.ts:329`), exactly the node `.jess` `$( … )` produces; and where the mode does NOT divide, the slash is a separator between two separate expressions, `$(lhs) / $(rhs)` (P34). A side with no math in it is not math and is not wrapped — `4 / 2` under the default mode is `4 / 2`, not `$(4) / $(2)`. WHERE THE SIDES SPLIT, owner 2026-09-24: asked whether, when the slash does not divide, everything on each side of it is that side's math — `@w: 4 / 2 + 5em;` → `4 / $(2 + 5em)`, and `@px * 2 / 4 * 3` → `$(@px * 2) / $(4 * 3)` — the owner answered *“correct!!!”*. That answer settles ONLY how a non-dividing slash splits its sides: it binds LOOSEST of the math operators, as a separator does (the P33 hierarchy), and the arithmetic on each side is that side's own `Expression`. The worked values shown with the question (`4 / 7em`, `20px / 12`) were examples, not a ruling on units; an earlier version of this row recorded `4 / 7em` as owner-confirmed, and the owner rejected that reading (2026-10-06). Whether a side's arithmetic computes is decided by the math and unit modes like any other operation. UNITLESS ± UNIT: see V27 — a unitless number adopts the other operand's unit in `+` and `-` in every unit mode, so the `4 / 2 + 5em` → `4 / 7em` example is simply correct, as are `border-radius-keep` (`8px / 7px`, golden proposal) and bootstrap's `((1.5 - 1rem) / 2)` → `0.25rem`; `@px * 2 / 4 * 3` with `@px: 10px` is `20px / 12`. HOW FAR EACH SIDE REACHES, owner 2026-09-24, asked whether the slash should group whole space-separated sides as css/.jess then did (`12px / [1.5 Arial]`): *“It's non-deterministic… I think just grouping the direct lhs value and rhs value with the slash is all we can really do. Properties are parsed individually so its probably safer than trying to group the whole side”*. So the slash binds LOOSER than the math operators and TIGHTER than spaces: a side is one space-separated value, including any math inside it — `a b/c + d e` is `[a, b / $(c + d), e]`. This applies in ALL FOUR dialects — owner, same day: *“so i think (12px/1.5) is the group (in CSS and all deriving languages)”* — and the equivalence rule requires the same shape anyway, which reverses the css rung order #264 introduced; P33 is amended to match. FIXTURES: the owner approved updating the Less fixtures whose output moves because an undivided slash stored in a variable is a list (`@d: 10px/2; @d * 2` → `calc(10px / 2 * 2)`; `calc(50% + (@v - 20px))` → `calc(50% + (50vh / 2 - 20px))`). DIVISION BY ZERO under `math: always` is an evaluation ERROR: the author opted into division, and there is no quotient to print (`0 / 0` verbatim would hide the mistake; `calc(0 / 0)` is NaN in CSS). Owner asked for a view; this was the recommendation, applied pending objection. MATH INSIDE `calc()` IS NOT SIMPLIFIED, in any dialect — owner 2026-09-24, verbatim: *“ok i didn't know this! so fair! let's not simplify”*, on being told that a math function's result is CLAMPED to the range the property allows and rounded where it needs an integer (css-values-4 §10.12), while a bare value is not: `padding: calc(1px - 5px)` is valid and resolves to `0`, `padding: -4px` invalidates the declaration; `z-index: calc(3 / 2)` rounds to `2`, `z-index: 1.5` is invalid. Jess does not know each property's range, so folding a `calc()` to a bare value can turn valid CSS into a dropped declaration. So Less `calc()` marks its operations `inMathFunction` exactly as css and `.jess` do: variables are substituted, the arithmetic stays written (`calc(@a * 2)` with `@a: 10px` → `calc(10px * 2)`), and every parenthesis authored inside the math function is kept as written, redundant or not — owner 2026-10-06, verbatim: *“no reason to drop parens. the user wanted to write it that way for a reason.”* AMENDED owner 2026-10-07, verbatim: *“in Less/Jess, parens are dropped IF the calculation in the parens is resolved.”* Parens authored inside a math function around math written there, or around a value nothing computes, are kept as written, redundant or not. A group whose content computes — a call a callable runs, a variable holding math that ran, a .jess `$( … )` — loses every level of parens around it: `@a: 10px; @b: 10px; calc(100% - ((min(@a + @b))))` → `calc(100% - 20px)`, while `calc(100% - (((@a + @b))))` → `calc(100% - (((10px + 10px))))`. A calc() whose argument is written as a paren group keeps the calc(); only the group's parens are dropped, so the result is still clamped: `calc((min(-5px, 1px)))` → `calc(-5px)`, `calc((percentage(0.5)))` → `calc(50%)`. Pin: `packages/jess/test/less/math-boundaries.test.ts` ‘drops the parens around a calculation resolved inside calc()’ (8f768a628, 710fff64b). This replaces the earlier rule here that kept only the parens that carry precedence: `calc(100% - (@a + @b))` keeps its inner parens, and so do `calc(100% - ((@a * 3) + (@a * 2)))` and `calc(((10vh)) + calc((5vh)))`. A `calc()` whose argument is a group around one value carries the group as that value's spelling (`calc((10px))` is `10px` spelled `(10px)`), so it prints the same in every position while a typed consumer still reads `10px`. The Less `calc` fixture lines that expected folding (`calc(10px * 2)` → `20px` and its siblings) are updated to the kept form under this ruling. This retires the rule that switched off all arithmetic beside a non-dividing slash (`withoutBareMath`, `less-parser/src/grammar-helpers.ts:675`, and the tests pinning `3 * 2 / 4`): its premise, that the whole slash group is authored bytes, is the separate-slash model P34 rejected. Under `math: always` the division computes (`@px / 2` → `5px`), since that is what the mode means. There is NO media-query exception: a `<ratio>` (`(aspect-ratio: 16/9)`) goes through the same division rule and the mode picks its shape like any other Less slash — `16 / 9` under the default mode, `1.7777777778` under `math: always`. THE INVARIANT this serves is the cross-dialect equivalence assertion in `docs/design/JESS-EQUIVALENCE-HARNESS.md`: `.less → .css` must equal `.less → .jess → .css`, byte for byte, both arms on jess's own engine. The harness now EXISTS (`emitJess` in `core/src/ast/emit-jess.ts`, a printer from the PARSED tree to `.jess` source, and the ratchet `packages/jess/test/jess/less-jess-equivalence.test.ts`, branch `feat/jess-source-emitter`). MEASURED at `origin/dev` 2026-09-23: the Less grammar wraps NO math in `Expression` today — its only `expression(` sites wrap CONDITIONS (`less-parser/src/grammar-helpers.ts:1263`) — so this is new structure. Emitted CSS moves exactly where the rulings in this row and P34 say it does; the AST oracle moves by design. Verbatim: *“that's... much harder... in .less, we have to respect the user request. MODERN MODE (any of the three present, in either spelling: Less-domain at-rules accept the dashed and undashed forms alike): there is no ambient Less function namespace, exactly as in `.jess` (P17). A Less built-in reaches the document only by import; an unimported call — including `min(-5px, 1px)` — is emitted verbatim, as an unknown CSS function is, and a CSS math function therefore keeps its clamping. This makes a modern-mode `.less` document and its `.jess` conversion agree on function scope directly, which is the equivalence rule (`.less → .css` == `.less → .jess → .css`). MEASURED at `origin/dev` 2026-09-25: no modern-mode concept exists in the code — Less built-ins are ambient in every Less document. SCOPE, owner-confirmed 2026-09-25 (*“correct, yes”*): the mode is decided per document, so a legacy partial `@import`ed into a modern document keeps its own ambient built-ins, and a modern partial stays modern inside a legacy one. PROJECT-WIDE SETTING, owner 2026-09-25: *“we should also make a config setting for this for all the .less files”*. So a Less compile option puts every `.less` file in modern mode regardless of its at-rules; its default is the per-document detection above. It lives beside `mathMode` / `unitMode` / `functionMode` in the Less options (`packages/config/src/types.ts`). The option's NAME and value spelling (`moduleMode: 'auto' | 'modern'` is the working name) are an agent choice, not an owner ruling. There is deliberately no value that forces legacy mode on a document that uses `@use`/`@compose`/`@export` — not asked for. So `#less` is an ALIAS the Less plugin provides for the package module `@jesscss/fns/less`, and both specifiers bind the same namespace, `less`; a leading `#` is not part of a derived namespace. The same holds in `.jess` (`@-use "#less"` binds `$less`). | A13 | **Remote (network) `@import` is BUILT, as an opt-in plugin behind an explicit host allowlist; the default stays OFF.** With no remote-import plugin configured nothing is fetched: a URL `@import` that may be CSS stays a CSS terminal, and one with no CSS meaning — `(inline)`, `(reference)`, `(less)`, `@-import`, `@compose` — is an error, since it cannot be a terminal. Opting in (`@jesscss/plugin-remote-import`, on the `canResolveImport → resolve → locate → getSource` pipeline) requires a non-empty host allowlist. The list names the hosts that are FETCHED AND INLINED, not the hosts a stylesheet may reference. Every fetch is `https:` only, with no cross-host redirects (same-origin, at most five), a 512 KiB body cap and a 5 s time cap. An allow entry that is an IP address is rejected, with no opt-in. A host that resolves to a private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, unspecified, benchmarking, multicast or reserved address (embedded-IPv4 IPv6 forms included) is refused. Classification follows the importing grammar's rules first, decided from the authored spelling at parse time (RESOLVED-SEMANTICS §12.3b): a URL written with a `.css` path or marked `(css)` is never fetched, on or off the list. Context passes each claim `mustLoad`. With the plugin configured: an allowed https URL is fetched as written, and an extensionless one is parsed in the importing file's language. An extensionless URL that is not fetched (off the list, IP literal, plain http) stays a CSS terminal (the Google Fonts case). Any other URL that is not fetched — one with an extension, or one that must load — is an `import/load-failed` error that `(optional)` does not suppress. HTTP 404/410 is `import/not-found`, which `(optional)` skips. An import that stays a CSS terminal keeps its media query on the `@import` (A10). `@use` and `@plugin` of a URL are refused before resolution, with or without the plugin. `@compose` of a URL follows the `@import` policy. Every path written inside a fetched document resolves against that document's URL in `Context._getPath` (`@import`, `(inline)`, `data-uri()`/`image-size()`, `@use`, `@plugin`); a path that does not land on the document's own host is an error. `data-uri()`/`image-size()` never fetch. `rewriteUrls`/`rootpath` apply inside a fetched document exactly as for a local import, with rewritten `url()`s rebased onto the document's URL. On Deno the same host list goes to `--allow-net`. A test PROVES Deno denies an off-list host with the app-level check disabled, and the plugin refuses to start under unrestricted `--allow-net`. | C19 | **Compile settings resolve per source file.** (1) Which settings: every `styles.config` from the file's own folder up to its package root is merged, the nearest winning setting by setting (O19); none is loaded for a file under `node_modules` (O20). The settings passed to the compiler, a render or `lessc` are merged over that, setting by setting (O13). The entry and every imported file resolve the same way, so a file's output never depends on which file imported it. Root definitions and root variable values are recorded per document at parse (`rememberDocumentContext`). Lookups run only when documents differ (`Context.mixedPolicies`). > **C15 migration shape.** First map the current `less` package entrypoints and
> the minimal Less runtime stack they require (`less-parser`, `jess-plugin-less`,
> Less fns, resolver/config/core pieces). Prefer a thin Less-only facade if more
> than one consumer needs the assembled Less compiler; otherwise put the generic
> primitive in core and keep the Less package's glue declarative. Move `less` to
> that Less-only assembly, add a package-graph check that rejects `less -> jess`,
> and leave `jess` as the batteries-included shell that imports the first-party
> language stack. Main risks: duplicating compiler setup between `jess` and
> `less`, accidentally reintroducing a merged function registry, or making a
> facade so broad that it becomes a second product shell.

> **C16 migration shape.** Short term, dialect plugins may still seed the
> transitional evaluator slot so Less alpha can move. The target is one function
> lookup path: root capability providers are attached above the stylesheet frame,
> block-local `@plugin` functions attach to their lexical frame, and function
> evaluation asks the function family on that frame chain before deciding whether
> a call is unknown, preserved, or eligible to fall back to variable/binding
> semantics. Do not move Less/Sass registries into `jess`, do not collapse
> functions into the variable/declaration map, and do not replace this with a
> broader host object. Keep the inherited-registry path lazy: ordinary frames
> should point at the nearest parent function scope (which may itself point at a
> parent/global scope) and allocate a local function map only when a plugin
> actually registers functions in that frame.

> **C14 key-materialization limitation (2026-07-24).** `scss-parser` lowers a map
> key to a Collection entry NAME (`string | Interpolation`; `mapKeyName` rejects
> every other key with `Unsupported SCSS map key`), so the key's own value type is
> not carried on the node and `evalCollection` recovers it through the
> `materialize` sniff. Every sniff branch preserves its input bytes verbatim, so
> this cannot move output — but it is a re-classification, and a quoted key has
> already lost its quotes at parse (harmless, since Sass string equality ignores
> quoting). The `key: ValueGroup` shape is deliberately wider than what the parser
> can currently produce so that lifting the parser restriction — the real fix —
> needs no change here. Colour, list, and map keys are unreachable until then.

> **C13 implementation state (verified 2026-07-24).** `packages/fns/src/` has the
> `shared/` + `less/` + `sass/` owner split and composed `less/index.ts` /
> `sass/index.ts`. It does **not** yet have the module-granular specifiers: the
> package `exports` map is only `.`, `./builtins`, and `./package.json`, and there
> is no `imports` map — so `#less` / `#sass/color` are the target, not the current
> shape. `src/builtins.ts` still exists as the frozen parity-evidence registry
> (C6) and is not the destination.
